project_scope.note: Core set follows the existing oak module in the Hays Botany ID tracker; expand later rather than forcing every Central Texas oak into the first pass.

priority: mature leaf shape AND underside texture
annual vs biennial acorn maturation when known
study_strategy.warning: Leaf shape alone can be misleading, especially in juvenile shoots and hybridizing oak populations.

quick_key.if: Subevergreen/live-oak habit + leathery narrow leaves + spindle-shaped acute acorn in a deep goblet/funnel cup
Deeply lobed deciduous leaf with sharp bristle/awn tips
Often cruciform leaf + thick yellowish hairy twigs + harsh stellate hairs beneath
Blue-green/glaucous obovate-elliptic leaves + pale papery bark + flattened barrel-like acorn
Low thicket-forming limestone shrub/small tree + flaky papery bark + very shallow saucer cupule
Narrow leathery leaves with a few coarse teeth + dark bark exfoliating in strips + tuberculate cupule

b065_study_strategy.warning: All four B065 taxa are Texas natives, but their native Texas ranges are eastern/coastal rather than the Central Texas target zone. Landscape occurrence around Austin/Hays does not make them target-zone native.

quick_split: Q. lyrata — overcup nearly encloses acorn; rounded-lobed white-oak leaf.
Q. michauxii — huge rounded-toothed leaf with gray pubescent underside; large sweet acorn.
Q. nigra — variable wedge/spatula-shaped leaf, often broad shallowly 3-lobed at tip.
Q. phellos — narrow willow-like entire leaves with a tiny bristle tip.
